base: main@63dac108 (rebased from 52c5e03e because LEGION-20 #975 bumped the daemon API contract to 2 and rewrote the same checkpoints.sh/checkpoints.test.sh/README regions; three files conflicted and were merged keeping both sides)
trickyParts: Dispatch caps GET /api/v1/issues/<key>/events?limit= at 200 (parseEventLimit), not the plan's 500; the relay pages at 200 and the fake Dispatch in the unit test rejects a larger limit with 400 so the cap cannot regress silently.

Within one tick the relay fetches events for every tracked key BEFORE discovering their children, then fetches the newly discovered keys, repeating per level: a root row that names a child was appended after that child's issue.created, so the child is always discovered in the same tick and its lower-id rows sort ahead of the row that named it (orderEvents by global id). Rig B's log shows the child's dispatch-4643 landing between the root's 4642 and 4645.

The envelope is a field-for-field port of publisher.go envelope()/payloadSummary including in_reply_to and urgency where the outbox sets them; the JetStream msgID is nats.go's `<dedupe_key>:<topic>` so a relay restart replays as duplicate=true and the daemon's consumed-event count does not move (proved live on rig A).
RELAY READY is logged after the first tick that fetched AND published without error, so RIG READY in isolated mode means the root's history is already in the rig NATS; the README/harness key on that.

The root-issue existence probe (GET /api/v1/issues/<root>, 404 -> RELAY UNHEALTHY exit 1) runs once inside the retry loop, so a Dispatch outage at boot is retried while a missing root is definitive; the events endpoint itself answers [] for an unknown key and would never expose that.

The unit test's fake sleep cannot tell a backoff from the poll interval by duration (the second backoff step is also 2000 ms): it classifies by whether the last log line is a RELAY RETRY, which is the contract the checkpoint precheck also relies on (newest `RELAY ` line).

Running the rig from a Legion worker pane: the pane's own LEGION_* identity (including LEGION_OMP_PATH, which up.sh would treat as an operator override) and TMUX must be scrubbed from the environment before up.sh, otherwise the smoke daemon inherits them; the throwaway launcher /tmp/legion61-rig.sh did that. Host load ~100/32 cores needed LEGION_WORKER_RPC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=60 and LEGION_WORKER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600 (documented daemon env keys, no code change) for controller/architect panes to complete their RPC handshake.

up.test.sh sources up.sh from a temp copy, so up.sh's repo_root there is `/` and the recorded relay command ends in `//scripts/smoke/issue-relay.ts`; the assertion compares against the sourced repo_root, exactly as the envoy-bridge argv is built.
deviations: Rebased onto main before the proof and before opening the PR (Sami's rule is rebase only on a real conflict): the rig daemon on the 52c5e03e base refused to boot against the installed pi-legion-envoy 1.23.0 (contract 2 vs required 1) and #975's rewrite of the same checkpoints/README regions made the branch conflict on GitHub anyway; the rebase produced 3 conflicted files, resolved by keeping both sides. `SMOKE_DISPATCH_INGRESS=rig` (main) and `isolated` (this change) coexist; the merged dispatch_ingress_block_reason names isolated, envoy, and rig. No fingerprint comment was posted because no PR existed yet.

Checkpoint 12 gained a `CHECKPOINT 12 OK: <root> released its admission slot and <queued> was promoted` line; it previously passed silently, contradicting the README's one-OK-line contract, and the harness case for 12 needed an observable pass.

The relay validates each Dispatch row with a passthrough zod schema at the boundary (repository rule: schema-parse outside data) and imports ISSUE_KEY_PATTERN from legion-state.ts rather than copying the regex; the plan described a plain cast.
EVENT_PAGE_LIMIT is 200 (Dispatch's maximum), not the plan's 500.

Two-rig proof was sequential (rig A, down, rig B) as the architect decided for spec v3: LEGION-41 (#1010) is not in main, so up.sh still hardcodes the legion-smoke-nats container name and listener machine id. The tester owns the concurrent run once #1010 lands. Both rigs' smoke architects were single-turn users of provider credit; rig A chose a single-issue tree (planner on the root), rig B decomposed into LEGSMOKE-124, so checkpoints 3 and 4 were exercised on both branches of main's new tree_progress/root_phase_worker logic.
